title: What do you think about Lynch's Eraserhead(And what this is more like - Tarkovsky or classical horror)

commenti.body: We dissected this picture in film class. It’s considered body horror. Lynch has said his pictures are often like a dream. I find the arguments for intentional symbolism in Eraserhead fascinating. A man not ready to be a man or a father. The Lady in the Radiator, her cheeks are filled with cum because she sucks up sperm, representing a wish that he had never impregnated his partner. The deformed baby as a symbol of his ineptitude and inferior sperm. I would suggest this film to anyone, especially if you are a member of a film viewing group that loves in-depth conversation after a viewing.
Yes, i understand that this is main idea of this fulm, but what about plot and narrativ?
I don't think you understand what the film implies if that is your question.
explain it to me than, please

What is good plot and narrative for you?

Because Eraserhead is definitely not interested in using traditional plot and narrative. It's meant to create a nightmare dreamscape where you cannot cling to logic.

It's worth noting that Kubrick referred to it as the greatest horror film ever made and screened it to cast and crew of The Shining.

Also neither Lynch not Tarkovsky have ever mentioned being influenced by the French New Wave as far as I'm aware of. For Lynch, its Hitchcock-Wilder-Fellini. For Tarkovsky it's Bergman-Bresson-Mizoguchi.

Lynch is a form of surrealist so his works are more like Bunuel/Dali’s Un Chien Andalou. I do think Eraserhead is more similar to The Shining in tone than Tarkovsky, both Eraserhead and the Shining have an otherworldly aura about them and you never quite know what’s going on. Eraserhead is far more surreal and enigmatic though. Tarkovsky is doing something else entirely- making poetic movies.

So movies can go beyond the plot or narrative. David Lynch especially is all about the mood and emotions he invokes. He is some part of the surrealist movement so his plots and narratives deliberately don't make a lot of "logical" sense, again it's all about the feelings and the themes he is going for.
Lol didnt Tarkovsky hate Bergman's films?

Absolutely not.

He included 3 Bergman movies in his top of all-time (Winter Light, Persona, Seventh Seal)

He also said the following "I am only interested in the views of two people: one is called Bresson and one called Bergman."
Oof I don't how I totally mixed up Bergman's distaste for Godard... disregard my comment.
Tarkovsky hated tons of filmmakers lmao I get the confusion
Tarkovsky was a Bergman stan to a point where he almost comes across as pathetic

>still not sure if this was a good or a bad movie. 

Trust your instinct! It is not a good or bad movie.

​

>Also I watched not so many horrors and best of watched was The Shining, but this is so different from Eraserhead.

It's not a horror movie either, although parts of it are scary. I see 

​

>inspirated by new French wave

Lynch saw film as an extension of his existing artistic practice that started with painting and also extends into sound design and music. He's more directly inspired by painters (Francis Bacon and Edward Hopper in particular) than filmmakers. In his autiobiography *Room to Dream* the only filmmaker I recall him mentioning more than once was Fellini.

I always remembered visiting my sister's apartment that had a radiator which made a light ringing sound when it was on and I found when I think more about some of the scenes from the movie that some of it must draw on everyday experiences made in an absurd way. Like the awkward conversation the main character has with his girlfriend's father at dinner or when tries to cut up the food during the dinner.

It’s probably his only film that I don’t like. I think his other films do a great job of jumping around on the edge of reality whereas Eraserhead doesn’t really let me wonder “what is real?”, which I love so much about his others.
